subtype: Approach: relying on the phone number memorised at home [Action]
passage: Every night for a month before the trip to the Stockholm summer market, Emil and his father, Javier, sang the phone number to the tune of a silly birthday song. "Oh-seven-three, four-four-one..." Emil thought it was a joke. Then, on the Saturday, in the crowd between the fish stalls and the flower carts, he lost his father's hand. He found the information booth with the big blue i. His legs were shaking, his voice was shaking, but when the woman asked for a number, the song came out on its own: "Oh-seven-three, four-four-one..." She dialled. Javier answered on the first ring. In a minute he was there, lifting Emil off the ground.

subtype: Approach: checking the rule that adults ask adults [Thinking]

Deepak slowed. He liked puppies. But a thought stopped him. "Grown-ups ask grown-ups. There's the tea shop right there with three men sitting in it. Why is he asking me?" He stepped back from the car. "Ask at the tea shop," he said loudly, and walked fast to his cousin Sarika's shop at the corner. He told her everything. Sarika stepped out and took down the car's number, called his mother, and that evening told the village head.

qa.q: Where did Deepak go after stepping back from the car?

qa.a: He kept his distance, spoke loudly and went straight to a trusted adult; it is also important never to go near or look into a stranger's car.

qa.a: Sarika takes it seriously at once, noting the car number, calling his mother and telling the village head the same day.

subtype: Approach: checking the rule that adults ask adults [Thinking]

subtype: Approach: family code word as a test [Action]
passage: At home we have a secret word. Only Ammi, Abbu, my Khala and my grandfather know it. Ammi said, "If anyone else says they've come to fetch you, ask for the word." He said, "Nazia, my beti, you did exactly right." That night he told the police and the school.
